questions.stem: A notebook runs pdf = orders.toPandas() on a 200-million-row table to loop over it in Python, and the driver runs out of memory. What's the cause, and the better fix?

options.text: toPandas caches the table on every node; unpersist the table first so memory is freed
toPandas brings every row to the driver; keep the work in Spark and write the result to a table
toPandas runs on one executor; add executors so the rows are spread across more of them
toPandas needs Arrow turned off; disable Arrow so the conversion streams rows to the driver

questions.explanation: Even with Arrow, toPandas() collects all records in the DataFrame to the driver program and should be done on a small subset of the data.

questions.stem: A sort-merge join of sales to customers is slow: one task runs far longer than the rest because one customer has 40% of the rows. Adaptive query execution is on. What does its skew handling do?

options.text: It switches the join to a broadcast join, because a skewed table counts as a small table
It drops the rows of the skewed key and logs them, so the rest of the join can finish
It retries the long task on the driver, which has more memory than the executors
It splits the skewed tasks, replicating if needed, into roughly evenly sized tasks

questions.explanation: AQE dynamically handles skew in sort merge join and shuffle hash join by splitting, and replicating if needed, skewed tasks into roughly evenly sized tasks.

questions.stem: When does adaptive query execution treat a partition as skewed, with the default settings?

options.text: When its task runs longer than the stage's other tasks combined, measured at runtime
When it holds more than 30 MB, the same size as the runtime broadcast threshold
When it's more than twice the average partition size, whatever its size in bytes
When it's more than 5 times the median partition size and larger than 256 MB

questions.explanation: A partition is skewed only when both are true: its size is more than skewedPartitionFactor (5) times the median partition size, and more than skewedPartitionThresholdInBytes (256MB).

questions.stem: The products table in that join is small, but Spark still shuffles the big sales table. Which change asks Spark to broadcast products instead?

options.text: A broadcast hint on the join, sales.join(broadcast(products), ...), or a higher autoBroadcastJoinThreshold
A repartition of products into one partition, so the join treats it as a single broadcast block
A lower spark.sql.shuffle.partitions, so the shuffle of sales turns into a broadcast by itself
A cache of the sales table, so the shuffle reads from memory and is no longer needed at all

questions.explanation: You can change the join type by setting spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold, or set a join hint with the DataFrame APIs: dataframe.join(broadcast(df2)).

questions.stem: Where does Fabric point out data skew in a Spark application, without you reading every task?

options.text: The lakehouse's table maintenance pane, which flags skewed tables before a join runs
The pipeline's run output, which reports skew for each notebook activity it started
The Spark advisor in the notebook's monitoring, which detects skew and shows an analysis
The capacity metrics app, which lists skewed partitions for each workspace's notebooks

questions.explanation: Data skew is a common issue; the Spark advisor supports skew detection, and if skew is detected, an analysis is displayed.
